# Decision history — lege-docwrite

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## docwrite.decision.export-formats

### Revision 1 — PDF is generated by Lege, IDML replaces native INDD, Markdown drops geometry

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.export-formats/1` · scope `all` · topic `export`

PDF is written directly through lege-pdf-write: deterministic, searchable (ToUnicode),
with embedded subset fonts, bookmarks from the book structure and page labels. Markdown
export keeps semantic structure (headings, emphasis, block quotes, images, links,
footnotes) and intentionally discards page geometry. InDesign interchange is IDML, not
native .indd: paragraph/character styles map to InDesign styles, chapter masters to parent
pages, the book flow to a threaded story, images/captions to anchored objects, footnotes to
InDesign footnotes. A later convenience command may ask a local InDesign to save the IDML
as .indd. EPUB is optional and late.

**Context.** IDML is Adobe's supported programmatic interchange format and InDesign opens it directly.

## docwrite.decision.incremental-pagination

### Revision 1 — Incremental pagination stops when page geometry converges

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.incremental-pagination/1` · scope `all` · topic `pagination`

Text lives in rope-backed stores (ropey) keyed by stable block IDs. Shaped paragraphs and
their line breaks are cached per block. After an edit, pagination restarts at the page
holding the edited paragraph and proceeds forward only until a page break lands on the
same block/line position as in the cached layout; from there the cached pages are reused
and only folios/running heads that depend on page numbers are refreshed lazily. A
keystroke on page 147 re-lays pages 147–148, not 149–400.

## docwrite.decision.pages-are-derived

### Revision 1 — Pages are derived; the semantic book model is canonical

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.pages-are-derived/1` · scope `all` · topic `document-model`

The canonical document is Book → Part → Chapter → Section → Block → Run with stable block
IDs. Blocks: body paragraph, chapter title, subhead, block quote, epigraph, image,
caption, verse, bibliography entry, section/scene break, and footnote/endnote references.
Runs carry bold, italic, small caps, super/subscript, language, link and citation
reference. Pages, lines and glyph positions are derived by typesetting and cached, never
stored as document content.

**Consequences.** A chapter that moves from page 73 to page 76 breaks nothing. Footnotes are modelled from the start even though page-local footnote placement lands in M4, because they complicate pagination and the model must not need reshaping later.

## docwrite.decision.persistence-bundle

### Revision 1 — A book is a .legebook directory bundle with atomic autosave and named snapshots

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.persistence-bundle/1` · scope `all` · topic `persistence`

A book is saved as a `.legebook` directory: a manifest (book metadata, structure order,
styles, masters, templates), one file per chapter holding its blocks and runs, an
`assets/` directory for images, a `sources/` directory for research records, and
`snapshots/` for named manuscript states. Every write goes to a temporary file and is
renamed into place; autosave runs off the typing path. Snapshots can be compared and
restored. The serialization format is chosen in M2 with diffability as a criterion.

**Consequences.** Reordering chapters rewrites only the manifest. A crash loses at most the unsaved edits since the last autosave tick.

## docwrite.decision.product-shape

### Revision 1 — A page-native book environment, not a lightweight Word

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.product-shape/1` · scope `all` · topic `product-shape`

lege-docwrite is a page-native book writing environment: the writer types directly into
a stable, typeset paged book, while the manuscript underneath is semantic structure that
stays easy to reorganize and export. Its basic nouns are book, chapter, paragraph, page,
source and style. The centre of the UI is the book itself (correctly sized pages stacked
with a small gap); a narrow left Book Map shows front matter, parts, chapters, sections and
back matter, and reordering there reorders the book; an optional right sidebar holds
styles, chapter properties, sources, notes or page settings; the top bar stays minimal.
Non-goals: real-time collaboration, track-changes workflows, mail merge, forms, tables
beyond simple ones, spreadsheets, free drawing, presentation features, macros, database
integration and Word compatibility.

**Context.** Scrivener structures manuscripts but compiles later; Vellum and Atticus format books but separate editing from the formatted preview; Ulysses is markup-first. The uncommon combination is: write directly into stable pages + semantic book structure + strong typography + very low latency + first-class research material + little office machinery.

**Consequences.** Feature requests are judged against the nouns above; anything that pulls toward a general office suite is out of scope by default.

## docwrite.decision.styles-masters-templates

### Revision 1 — Styles, page masters and chapter templates are three separate systems

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.styles-masters-templates/1` · scope `all` · topic `style-systems`

Paragraph and character styles (Body, First Paragraph, Chapter Title, Section Heading,
Block Quote, Epigraph, Footnote, …) define text appearance. Page masters (Chapter Opener,
Left Body, Right Body, Part Divider, Front Matter, Bibliography, …) define page geometry,
running heads and folios. Chapter templates (Chapter, Part, Introduction, Appendix,
Bibliography, …) bind them: start on next page or next recto, number style, vertical start
position, title style, optional subtitle/epigraph, first-paragraph indent, running-head
behaviour and opener folio visibility. A chapter references its template; changing the
template changes every chapter that uses it.

**Context.** This is the lesson from InDesign's parent pages and styles without its free-object layout model.

## docwrite.decision.text-stack

### Revision 1 — Book text is shaped with harfrust and skrifa, broken with unicode-linebreak and hypher

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.text-stack/1` · scope `all` · topic `text-stack`

docwrite-typeset shapes with harfrust (OpenType GSUB/GPOS with feature selection: kern,
liga, smcp, c2sc, onum, pnum, …), reads outlines and metrics with skrifa (shared with
pdf-font), segments with unicode-segmentation, resolves direction with unicode-bidi,
finds break opportunities with unicode-linebreak and hyphenates with hypher. Glyphs are
rasterized through pixelkit's RasterKernel into a per-glyph atlas cache owned by docwrite,
keyed by (font, glyph, size, subpixel offset), so editing never re-rasterizes whole
paragraphs. TrueType and CFF-flavoured OpenType fonts are both supported.

## docwrite.decision.ui-stack-pixelkit

### Revision 1 — The app is hosted on pixelkit; viewer ideas are ported, not depended on

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.ui-stack-pixelkit/1` · scope `all` · topic `ui-stack`

docwrite-app uses pixelkit-shell (winit host, redraw on demand, Waker, Presenter seam,
frame log), pixelkit-raster (Painter, clip stack, RasterKernel) and pixelkit-ui (sidebar,
toolbar and dialog widgets). The page canvas and its multi-line rich-text editing are
docwrite's own. From lege-viewer, these are ported by copy and adaptation rather than
linked: scroll/anchor.rs (ReadingAnchor), frame.rs (FrameScheduler), damage.rs,
diagnostics.rs (FrameMetrics), trace.rs (input-trace record/replay) and the
tests/architecture.rs style of behaviour gates. The viewer's conductor and tile pipeline
are not reused: they assume read-only, rasterize-once content.

**Context.** Chosen by the user on 2026-09-23. lege-viewer is one application crate, not a toolkit, and its engine enums are closed over PDF artifacts. A wgpu presenter can be added later through pixelkit's Presenter seam once that seam is injectable.

**Consequences.** pixelkit needs upstream patches before M1 (see the pixelkit namespace). pixelkit-text is used only for UI chrome, not for book typesetting.

## docwrite.decision.workspace-home

### Revision 1 — lege-docwrite is a nested Cargo workspace tracked by the Lege-ecosystem repository

`proposed` · `@docwrite.decision.workspace-home/1` · scope `all` · topic `repo-home`

lege-docwrite lives at Lege-ecosystem/lege-docwrite as its own Cargo workspace (own
lockfile and target/), excluded from the ecosystem root, tracked by the parent git
repository, with its own AKR ledger and codegraph index. It consumes lege-pdf-write,
lege-pdf-read, pdf-font and pdf-text by path, and the pixelkit crates from the sibling
../pixelkit checkout. Crates: docwrite-model (book tree, styles, masters, templates, edit
transactions and undo), docwrite-typeset (shaping, breaking, pagination), docwrite-export
(PDF, Markdown, IDML) and docwrite-app (binary lege-docwrite). A research crate is added in
M4. Generic UI pieces are extracted from lege-viewer or pushed into pixelkit only once
docwrite demonstrates they are shared.

**Context.** Chosen by the user on 2026-09-23, following the lege-pdf/pdf-integrity pattern. The ecosystem root's [patch] entries do not carry over into this workspace.
